# Migrations

## Product (this repo)

Revisions live in `migrations/versions/` and carry the `product` branch label.
Create them with:

```bash
uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "description"
```

### Always read an autogenerated revision before committing it

Two traps have already bitten this codebase:

**Renames preserve index names.** `op.rename_table` and `op.alter_column` rename
the object but *not* dependent indexes, and autogenerate *does* compare index
names. If you rename an entity, rename its indexes explicitly:

```python
op.execute("ALTER INDEX idx_usuario_prefeitura RENAME TO idx_usuario_organizacao")
```

That is a catalog-only operation — no rebuild. Skip it and the *next*
autogenerated revision silently proposes dropping and recreating production
indexes, in a diff nobody thinks to question.

**Backfills must survive non-empty tables.** A migration tested only against an
empty dev database proves nothing. Before shipping one that backfills a column
under a unique constraint, insert adversarial rows and round-trip it:

```bash
uv run alembic downgrade -1
# insert rows that collide, truncate, or are empty
uv run alembic upgrade head
uv run alembic downgrade -1
uv run alembic upgrade head
```

A `downgrade()` also has to survive the data its own `upgrade()` made possible —
if the upgrade relaxes a constraint, the downgrade must backfill before
restoring it.

### Known defect: `downgrade base` does not work

Inherited from the municipal product. `20260408_0237_dcc0d379db3c_expand_instituicao_for_external_catalog_.py`
calls `op.create_foreign_key(None, ...)` and `op.drop_constraint(None, ...)` —
an autogenerate artifact that never got a real constraint name. Downgrading
through it raises:

```
CompileError: Can't emit DROP CONSTRAINT for constraint ForeignKeyConstraint(...); it has no name
```

Stepwise downgrades (`downgrade -1`) work fine; only a full unwind to `base`
fails. To rebuild a dev database from scratch, drop and recreate the schema
instead:

```bash
PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h localhost -p 5433 -U postgres -d buska_db <<'SQL'
DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE;
CREATE SCHEMA public;
GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO buska_user;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp";
SQL
uv run alembic upgrade head
```

Note the superuser: the app role cannot create extensions. Also note that
`psql -c "a; b; c"` runs as one implicit transaction — if any statement fails,
the whole thing silently rolls back. Use a heredoc, or separate `-c` flags.

The same defect exists in `municipal-backend`, which *has* deployments, so fixing
it there requires care. This repo has none, so it can be corrected whenever
convenient.

## Client deployments (mebuska-deploy)

Client repos add their own directory and never write into `migrations/versions/`:

```ini
# mebuska-deploy/alembic.ini
version_locations = %(here)s/migrations/paqtcpb <path-to-installed-product>/migrations/versions
```

Client revisions set `down_revision` to a *product* revision ID and declare their
own label:

```python
branch_labels = ("paqtcpb",)
```

New product migrations then merge in without touching client migrations.

Check for accidental head splits with `alembic heads` — more than one head per
branch label means someone branched by mistake. A healthy tree looks like:

```
$ uv run alembic heads
a1b2c3d4e5f7 (product) (head)
```

See `docs/plugins.md` for the rest of the client extension contract.
